purpose: Offline quality cases for the GEO drug-value integration. Rubrics guide review, never block a live delivery. Engineering checks run separately from model-quality evaluation.
modelEvaluation: Not claimed by passing engineering tests. Run these briefs with preserved project material and assess the actual outputs against each case rubric.

cases.brief: Plan GEO for a medicine known only by its generic name. The brand and formulation are ambiguous; disease-level research is available.
review: Continue supported molecule/disease analysis
State identity limits; do not infer brand equivalence
Ask only the identity question needed for product-specific work

cases.brief: We have a label and two small studies, no comparative trial and no local prices. Find useful GEO opportunities.
review: Preserve partial six-perspective analysis
No invented total score, cost-effectiveness or superiority
Prioritize supportable decisions without filling every field

cases.brief: A caregiver reports difficulty administering treatment; a pharmacist reports monitoring burden. Map useful questions, including switching and stopping.
review: Use caregiver and pharmacist perspectives
Distinguish observed reports from inferred demand
Allow nonlinear decisions and overlapping subgroups

cases.brief: Social crawling failed. New guideline information, medicine availability problems and contradictory review findings are available.
review: Discover non-social opportunities
Preserve typical questions as inferred
No fabricated real quotations or mandatory number of questions

cases.brief: Position an established generic against a new formulation with different trial populations and a non-drug alternative.
review: Compare clinical decisions and applicability
Novelty is not proven innovation
No unsupported cross-trial ranking

cases.brief: Choose work for a limited budget: a clinically important safety question, an easy visibility gain and an unresolved reimbursement question.
review: Explain importance, value, gap, feasibility and effort
Reuse completed research before requesting more
Do not invent weighted clinical scores or ROI

cases.brief: A widely cited marketing story appears on ten syndicated sites while the original trial is rarely cited. Choose sources and channels.
review: Separate clinical credibility from retrieval
Syndication does not add independent studies
Match audience and topic with spending still authorized separately

cases.brief: Adapt the plan for an early medicine with uncertain long-term outcomes versus a mature OTC treatment.
review: Choose methods proportionate to lifecycle and evidence
Avoid forcing every specialist or a fixed pipeline
Preserve reasonable non-recommendation

cases.brief: An adverse-event analysis found a reporting signal. Write a patient-facing answer and a pharmacist discussion without estimating incidence from reports.
review: Reporting signals are not incidence, causality or comparative safety ranking
Balance benefits and harms with known scope
Keep missing inputs local to the unsupported calculation

cases.brief: Write a useful explanation about monitoring and caregiver burden from qualitative evidence with no valid effect estimate.
review: Useful content without forced statistics, quote or word count
Audience-specific framing from shared findings
Keep uncertainty and treatment conditions

cases.brief: Costs differ by region, insurance status and time. We know only one payer price. Explain patient affordability and access.
review: Distinguish out-of-pocket, budget impact and cost-effectiveness
No extrapolation from one payer price to all patients
Missing costs remain unknown

cases.brief: A safety specialist timed out after writing a usable report. The subgroup calculation failed, and the GEO article batch is waiting.
review: Reuse usable report and original files
Explain missing subgroup calculation without erasing results
No recursive queue or automatic retry loop

cases.brief: Brand mentions increased but the answers omitted the studied population and overstated safety. Prepare the weekly interpretation.
review: Read semantic observations and clinical context with traditional metrics
Distinguish exposure from accurate value uptake
No claim of clinical outcome improvement

cases.brief: A new source changes one finding after the baseline. Two engines were measured on different question versions; a third refused.
review: Freeze one profile version for the package
Compare like engine, question-set, time and rubric only
Unknown/refused answers are not zeros; keep control/noise limits

cases.brief: An updated label affects one safety finding and two articles. Other effectiveness findings are unchanged.
review: Review explicit affected links selectively
Keep historical versions readable
Do not globally withhold or regenerate all work

cases.brief: A simpler explanation improves answer uptake, while the clinical evidence remains uncertain. Summarize what should carry into the next project.
review: Learn a scoped communication method with observed outcome
GEO performance does not upgrade scientific certainty
Preserve researcher ownership and source provenance
